before.known: I'm not going to explain what I mean
before.target: nílim chun triail a mhíniú cad atá i gceist agam

after.target: nílim chun cad atá i gceist agam a mhíniú

problem: Meaning/grammar: the target inserts 'triail' ('try'), which the English does not say, and the word order is wrong.
evidence: 'a mhíniú' is the verb taking 'cad atá i gceist agam' as its object; 'triail a mhíniú' is ungrammatical and adds a meaning.

before.known: I do not know if I can remember the whole sentence
before.target: Ní aithním an féidir liom an abairt iomlán a chuimhneamh

problem: Wrong word: 'aithním' means 'I recognise/know a person', not 'I don't know if'.
evidence: The seed 85 sense is knowing people. 'Níl a fhios agam' is the course's phrase for knowing facts.

before.known: I do not know how to say enough different words yet
before.target: Ní aithním conas go leor focail éagsúla a rá fós

problem: Wrong verb: 'Ní aithním' for 'I do not know how to say'.
evidence: 'Níl a fhios agam conas' is used elsewhere in the course, e.g. S0088L05B01.

before.known: I do not know what I am looking for
before.target: Ní aithním cad atá mé ag lorg

problem: Wrong verb: 'Ní aithním' for 'I do not know what I am looking for'.
evidence: 'aithním' is for knowing a person, not for knowing a fact.

before.known: I do not know if I can help you at the same time as doing this
before.target: Ní aithním an féidir liom cabhrú leat ag an am céanna

problem: Wrong verb, and the target omits 'as doing this' from the English.
evidence: The English says 'I do not know if I can help you at the same time as doing this'. The target is 'Ní aithním an féidir liom cabhrú leat ag an am céanna'.

before.known: I do not know if I can remember the whole sentence, but I am going to try
before.target: Ní aithním an féidir liom an abairt iomlán a chuimhneamh, ach tá mé chun triail a dhéanamh

problem: Wrong verb: 'Ní aithním' for 'I do not know if'.
evidence: 'aithním' means recognising a person, as in the seed 'Ní aithním na daoine sin'.

before.known: I do not know how to say enough different words in Irish yet
before.target: Ní aithním conas go leor focail éagsúla a rá fós

problem: Wrong verb: 'Ní aithním' for 'I do not know how to say'. The English also has 'in Irish', which the target lacks.
evidence: This duplicates B05 with the same error.

before.known: I do not know those people, but I am not going to stop talking
before.target: Ní aithním na daoine sin, ach níl mé ag iarraidh stopadh ag caint

problem: Meaning mismatch: 'I am not going to stop talking' is rendered 'níl mé ag iarraidh stopadh ag caint' ('I don't want to stop talking').
evidence: The English 'going to' corresponds to 'chun' in the target.

before.known: I do not know when I will be ready to meet people tonight
before.target: Ní aithním cathain a bheidh mé réidh bualadh le daoine anocht

problem: Wrong verb: 'Ní aithním' for 'I do not know when'.
evidence: The target also drops 'le labhairt'.

before.known: I do not know how to say what I want to say in Irish yet
before.target: Ní aithním conas a rá cad a bhí mé ag iarraidh a rá i nGaeilge fós

problem: Wrong verb, garbled word order, and the tense does not match ('bhí mé ag iarraidh' for 'I want').
evidence: The target is 'conas a rá cad a bhí mé ag iarraidh a rá', against the English 'how to say what I want to say'.

before.known: I do not know those people, and I was not thinking about how to give an answer
before.target: Ní aithním na daoine sin, agus ní raibh mé ag smaoineamh ar conas freagra a thabhairt

problem: The target uses 'ar conas' and says 'ag smaoineamh ar conas freagra a thabhairt' for 'how to give an answer'. It is stilted, and the wrong 'ní aithním' sense is used.
evidence: The first clause is fine, but the second clause is garbled.

before.known: I do not know when I will be ready to speak Irish well
before.target: Ní aithním cathain a bheidh mé réidh labhairt i nGaeilge go maith

problem: Wrong verb: 'Ní aithním' for 'I do not know when'. The English and target also differ ('Irish well' vs 'i nGaeilge go maith').
evidence: 'Níl a fhios agam' would be the correct verb.

before.known: I do not know those people, but I am starting to practise talking to people
before.target: Ní aithním na daoine sin, ach tá mé ag tosú ag labhairt a chleachtadh

problem: Meaning mismatch: the English says 'practise talking to people' but the target says 'ag tosú ag labhairt a chleachtadh', which is ungrammatical.
evidence: 'tá mé ag tosú ag labhairt a chleachtadh' is a doubled verbal-noun construction.

before.known: I do not know those people, but she told me they speak Irish very well
before.target: Ní aithním na daoine sin, ach dúirt sí liom go bhfuil siad ag labhairt Gaeilge go han-mhaith

problem: Meaning mismatch: 'she told me they speak Irish very well' is rendered 'dúirt sí liom go bhfuil siad ag labhairt Gaeilge go han-mhaith'. The tense differs too, because the English is habitual and the target is progressive.
evidence: Habitual 'labhraíonn' is needed.

before.known: I do not know what I am supposed to do, but I am going to try my best
before.target: Ní aithním cad atá le déanamh agam, ach tá mé ag iarraidh mo dhícheall a dhéanamh

problem: Wrong verb, and the meaning is off: 'what I am supposed to do' vs 'cad atá le déanamh agam'. The second clause 'tá mé ag iarraidh' differs from 'I am going to try'.
evidence: 'Ní aithním' is for people, not facts.

before.known: I haven't started to feel better yet, but I haven't been sleeping well and that is part of the problem
before.target: Níl mé ag tosú ag mothú níos fearr fós, ach ní bhainim taitneamh as dúiseacht nuair nár chodail mé go maith

problem: Meaning mismatch: the target 'ní bhainim taitneamh as dúiseacht nuair nár chodail mé go maith' does not say what the English says ('I haven't been sleeping well and that is part of the problem').
evidence: The English says 'I haven't started to feel better'. The target says 'I don't enjoy waking when I didn't sleep well'.

before.known: I'm not able to remember easily yet, but I'm not worried about making mistakes because I think it is a good thing
before.target: Ní bheidh mé ábalta cuimhneamh go héasca fós, ach ní bhíonn imní orm faoi botúin a dhéanamh mar ceapaim gur rud maith é

problem: Tense and meaning mismatch: 'Ní bheidh mé ábalta' is future ('I won't be able'), but the English is present ('I'm not able').
evidence: The English also has 'I'm not worried', while the target has 'ní bhíonn imní orm', which is habitual.

before.known: we still haven't managed to meet together, and I wasn't even thinking about how to make that happen tonight
before.target: Ní raibh muid ag iarraidh bualadh le chéile fós, agus ní raibh mé ag smaoineamh ar conas é sin a dhéanamh anocht

problem: Meaning mismatch: 'we still haven't managed to meet' is rendered 'Ní raibh muid ag iarraidh bualadh le chéile fós' ('we didn't want to meet').
evidence: The English also says 'I wasn't even thinking about'.

before.known: she doesn't want to read anything this evening yet, because she is feeling a little tired this morning
before.target: Níl sí ag iarraidh aon rud a léamh tráthnóna inniu fós, ach tá sí beagán tuirseach ar maidin

problem: Meaning mismatch: the English says 'this evening yet' and 'this morning', but the target says 'tráthnóna inniu' and 'ar maidin'. The conjunction 'because' is rendered 'ach' ('but').
evidence: The English says 'because she is feeling a little tired'. The target says 'ach tá sí beagán tuirseach'.

before.known: he thinks that there is something he still needs to do before he is ready to come back to meet everyone later
before.target: ceapaim go bhfuil rud éigin air le déanamh fós sula mbeidh sé réidh teacht ar ais le gach duine eile níos déanaí

problem: Meaning mismatch: the English says 'he thinks' but the target 'ceapaim' means 'I think'. The phrase also has 'air le déanamh' for 'he still needs to do'.
evidence: The target subject is first person while the English subject is third person.

before.known: I think that there is no need to worry, because I know that making mistakes is a very good thing when you're learning
before.target: ceapaim go bhfuil sé maith gan imní a bheith ort, mar ceapaim gur rud maith é botúin a dhéanamh

problem: The target 'ceapaim go bhfuil sé maith gan imní a bheith ort' does not match the English 'there is no need to worry'.
evidence: The English says 'there is no need to worry'. The target says 'it is good not to be worried'.

before.known: I think that there is enough already done, and I feel that we should be happy with what we have achieved so far
before.target: ceapaim go bhfuil go leor déanta cheana féin, agus mothaím go bhfuil mé an-sásta leis an méid atá foghlamtha againn

problem: Meaning mismatch: the English says 'we should be happy' but the target says 'mothaím go bhfuil mé an-sásta ... againn' ('I feel I am happy').
evidence: Person and mood differ between the two sides.

before.known: I know that there is a lot of interesting things to do today, but I'm not sure yet what I want to start with
before.target: Tá a fhios agam go bhfuil go leor rudaí suimiúla le déanamh inniu, ach níl mé cinnte fós cad atá mé ag lorg

problem: Meaning mismatch: the second clause 'what I want to start with' is rendered 'cad atá mé ag lorg' ('what I am looking for').
evidence: The English and the target mean different things.

before.known: I think that there is still more to find out about this story, and I want to know the truth before anyone else does
before.target: ceapaim go bhfuil fós níos mó le fáil amach faoin scéal seo, agus tá mé ag iarraidh an fhírinne a chloisteáil

problem: Meaning mismatch: 'to know the truth before anyone else' is rendered 'an fhírinne a chloisteáil' ('to hear the truth') and the 'before anyone else' clause is dropped.
evidence: The target omits part of the English.

before.known: I feel that there is something very enjoyable about the moment you start to understand more words in Irish
before.target: mothaím go bhfuil rud éigin suimiúil faoin am nuair a thuigeann tú go leor focail as Gaeilge

problem: Meaning mismatch: the target 'faoin am nuair a thuigeann tú go leor focail as Gaeilge' differs from the English, and 'as Gaeilge' is wrong.
evidence: The English says 'enjoyable' but the target says 'suimiúil' ('interesting').

before.known: I know that there is something wonderful about the surprise of discovering how much you already understand
before.target: Tá a fhios agam go bhfuil rud éigin suimiúil faoi ionadh a bheith ort nuair a thuigeann tú go leor cheana féin

problem: Meaning mismatch: the English talks about 'the surprise of discovering how much you already understand'. The target 'faoi ionadh a bheith ort nuair a thuigeann tú go leor cheana féin' is garbled, and 'suimiúil' does not mean 'wonderful'.
evidence: The English says 'wonderful' but the target says 'suimiúil'.

before.known: I'm pleased with everything I've done today, but I know there is still a lot more I need to learn before I'm ready
before.target: Tá mé sásta leis gach rud atá déanta agam inniu, ach tá a fhios agam go bhfuil fós go leor le foghlaim agam sula mbeidh mé réidh

problem: Grammar: 'leis gach rud' is ungrammatical, since it should be 'le gach rud'. The English also says 'there is still a lot more I need to learn', which the target does not match.
evidence: The same error appears in S0089L05U04.

before.known: I'm surprised by everything that has been done already, and I think we should feel good about how far we have come
before.target: Tá ionadh orm le gach rud atá déanta cheana féin, agus ceapaim gur rud maith é sin a chloisteáil

problem: Meaning mismatch: the second clause 'we should feel good about how far we have come' is rendered 'ceapaim gur rud maith é sin a chloisteáil' ('I think it is good to hear that').
evidence: The English and the target mean different things.

before.known: there is already a lot done today, and I feel that it's important to take time to appreciate how much progress we've made
before.target: Tá go leor déanta cheana féin inniu, agus mothaím go bhfuil sé tábhachtach am a thógáil le feiceáil cé mhéad atá foghlamtha againn

problem: Meaning mismatch: 'appreciate how much progress we've made' is rendered 'am a thógáil le feiceáil cé mhéad atá foghlamtha againn'. The target is garbled and its meaning differs from the English.
evidence: The English talks about progress. The target talks about what has been learned.

before.known: I want to keep going until I've done everything I set out to do today, and I'm not going to stop until then
before.target: Tá mé ag iarraidh leanúint ar aghaidh go dtí go mbeidh gach rud déanta agam inniu, agus nílim chun stopadh go dtí sin

problem: Meaning mismatch: 'nílim chun stopadh go dtí sin' omits 'until then' as expressed in the English, and the first clause says 'Tá mé ag iarraidh leanúint ar aghaidh go dtí go mbeidh gach rud déanta agam', which is not a close match.
evidence: The English says 'I've done everything I set out to do today'.

before.known: I think everything that has been done so far is excellent, and I'm very happy with all the progress we've all made together
before.target: ceapaim go bhfuil gach rud atá déanta go dtí seo go han-mhaith, agus tá mé an-sásta leis an méid atá foghlamtha againn le chéile

problem: Meaning mismatch: 'is excellent' is rendered 'go han-mhaith', which is an adverb and ungrammatical here.
evidence: 'ceapaim go bhfuil gach rud atá déanta go dtí seo go han-mhaith' is not grammatical as a predicate.

before.known: I don't know how to say most of the words I have in my head when I try to speak to someone new in Irish
before.target: Níl a fhios agam conas a rá na focail atá agam i mo cheann nuair atá mé ag triail labhairt le duine nach n-aithním as Gaeilge

problem: Meaning mismatch: the target 'conas a rá na focail atá agam i mo cheann' is ungrammatical, and 'duine nach n-aithním as Gaeilge' is wrong for 'someone new in Irish'.
evidence: The English says 'someone new'. The target says 'someone I don't know'.

before.known: I know the worry I have is about not knowing enough words yet, but I think that's something everyone feels at the start
before.target: Tá a fhios agam go bhfuil imní agam nach bhfuil go leor focail agam fós, ach ceapaim gur rud maith é sin a chloisteáil

problem: Meaning mismatch: 'ceapaim gur rud maith é sin a chloisteáil' means 'I think it is good to hear that', not 'that's something everyone feels at the start'.
evidence: The English says 'I know the worry I have is about not knowing enough words yet'.

before.known: I'm not sure how much time I have left before I have to leave, but I want to keep practising for as long as possible
before.target: Níl mé cinnte cé mhéad ama atá agam sula gcaithfidh mé imeacht, ach tá mé ag iarraidh labhairt a chleachtadh chomh luath agus is féidir liom

problem: Meaning mismatch: 'for as long as possible' is rendered 'chomh luath agus is féidir liom' ('as soon as I can').
evidence: The English says 'for as long as possible'.

before.known: I know there is a lot I have already achieved, and I think that is something really worth remembering and feeling good about
before.target: Tá a fhios agam go bhfuil go leor déanta agam cheana féin, agus ceapaim gur rud maith é sin a chuimhneamh

problem: Meaning mismatch: 'worth remembering and feeling good about' is rendered 'gur rud maith é sin a chuimhneamh', which is ungrammatical and does not match.
evidence: The English and the target differ.

before.known: there is a lot that I know already and that makes me very happy, because I wasn't sure I could manage at the start
before.target: Tá go leor agam atá foghlamtha cheana féin agus tá ionadh orm cé chomh maith agus atá mé ag déanamh anois

problem: Meaning mismatch: the target 'tá ionadh orm cé chomh maith agus atá mé ag déanamh anois' does not say what the English says (I'm very happy because I wasn't sure I could manage).
evidence: The English and the target say different things.

before.known: I think there is a lot that is interesting about Irish, and I want to learn it and speak it with as many people as I can
before.target: ceapaim go bhfuil go leor suimiúil faoi Gaeilge a fhoghlaim, agus tá mé ag iarraidh labhairt le daoine a labhraíonn Gaeilge

problem: Meaning mismatch: 'go leor suimiúil faoi Gaeilge a fhoghlaim' is ungrammatical, and 'speak it with as many people as I can' is not what the target says.
evidence: The English and the target say different things.

before.known: I know there is a lot to practise and I want to do my best every day and try to keep going for as long as possible
before.target: Tá a fhios agam go bhfuil go leor le triail agam agus tá mé ag iarraidh mo dhícheall a dhéanamh inniu agus leanúint ar aghaidh ar feadh tamaill

problem: Meaning mismatch: 'go bhfuil go leor le triail agam' is wrong for 'there is a lot to practise', and 'inniu' replaces 'every day'.
evidence: The English says 'every day'. The target says 'inniu'.

before.known: I know there is a lot to understand when you're learning Irish, but I think it's really enjoyable when you get it
before.target: Tá a fhios agam go bhfuil go leor le tuiscint nuair atá tú ag foghlaim Gaeilge, ach ceapaim gur rud maith é

problem: Meaning mismatch: the second clause 'it's really enjoyable when you get it' is rendered 'ceapaim gur rud maith é' ('I think it is a good thing').
evidence: The English and the target say different things.

before.known: I know there is a lot to say, and I want to find the right way to say it in Irish so that you understand what I mean
before.target: Tá a fhios agam go bhfuil go leor le rá agam, agus tá mé ag lorg conas rud éigin a rá i nGaeilge le cad atá i gceist agam a mhíniú

problem: Meaning mismatch: the target 'tá mé ag lorg conas rud éigin a rá i nGaeilge le cad atá i gceist agam a mhíniú' is garbled and does not match the English.
evidence: The English says 'find the right way to say it in Irish so that you understand what I mean'.
